newsitem.title: UK: European bonds' advantage over US seen short-lived.
newsitem.headline: European bonds' advantage over US seen short-lived.

text.p: European bond markets managed to outperform their U.S. counterparts on Friday after a mixed U.S. labour report, but analysts said the advantage may be eroded.
The June Bund future initially inched up but then lost ground to trade at 99.30 by 1350 GMT. Gilts also rose just after the data but then edged back to 108-19.
With U.S. Treasuries coming off slightly after the data, the 10-year T-note/Bund spread widened six basis points to 102 bps.
"We're outperforming the U.S. at the moment but I don't think that will be sustained," said Sonja Gibbs, senior bond strategist at Nomura International here.
"The European recovery is likely to pick up in the next few months too and there will be little opportunity for decoupling. We will just be following the U.S. market down," said Gibbs.
U.S. non-farm payrolls rose 175,000 in March, lower than the expected 196,000. Unemployment edged down to 5.2 percent, which was in line with expectations.
Traders on LIFFE were also sceptical about the durability of any European rally.
"They were really nothing figures. It will die a death as soon as the initial orders are through," said a trader at a U.S. bank.

The Bund market was declared a fast market as soon as the figures came out with prices in the pit moving too fast to register electronically. Traders said after the initial rally had run its course there was little to support further gains.
They said Bunds were following T-bonds blindly and were likely to stall as soon as Treasuries calmed.
Bond markets fluctuated immediately after the data, with the latest declines triggered by a fall through key technical support levels, traders added.
Graham McDevitt, head of bond research at Paribas Capital Markets here, was bullish on European markets short term.
"We will see a squeeze higher in the next two to four weeks," McDevitt said. "A lot of long positions in the market have been squeezed out."
Beyond the two to four week view, he said the trend in European bonds was down. "EMU is still looking quite messy."
The 10-year T-note/Bund spread has been largely above 100 basis points since the U.S. Federal Reserve raised the federal funds target rate to 5.50 percent on March 25.
Prior to Friday's data, it had narrowed to 96 basis points.
But McDevitt said European markets would not start to squeeze upward until some levels were broken, and traders on LIFFE said that in the current environment sellers held sway.
"Even though we have broken through 99.28 on the Bund, we might have made a bottom for a short time. It has to get above 99.70 for the squeeze up to get going to 100.50," said McDevitt.
LIFFE dealers said that during the initial moments after the data the market left significant gaps.
This meant that when prices turned, the slide was especially fast. Arbitrage players of T-bonds and DTB futures were heavy sellers and downward pressure also came from U.S. houses.
"It seemed like for every one good piece of news we had one bad and when the T-bonds touched 107-02, things looked really bad," said a trader at a European bank on LIFFE.
She said the Bunds would have to recover above 99.58 to abort the bear trend.
There was further to go all the way down to 98.68, she said, while on the T-bonds a break of 107-02 would see 106-22 reached quickly.
By 1424 GMT, June T-bonds were near the session low, trading 15/32 down at 107-05. June Bunds were at 99.18, down 0.06 and off from a 99.51 high.
-- Jennifer Scott, Carolyn Cohn, Bonds +44 171 542 8682
